t: Aksum, in highland Ethiopia and Eritrea, grew rich trading African ivory and gold through its Red Sea port of Adulis.
Under King Ezana it became one of the first states to adopt Christianity, founding Ethiopia's Orthodox tradition.
Cut off from Red Sea trade by Persia and the early Islamic conquests, it shrank into a regional highland kingdom.
dyk: Aksum was one of the very few ancient states to mint its own gold coins, and the first to place the Christian cross on its coinage.
ev: King Endubis introduces Aksumite gold, silver and bronze coinage
King Ezana conquers the Kingdom of Kush, reaching the Nile
King Kaleb's seaborne expedition overthrows the Himyarite king Dhu Nuwas in Yemen
A Sasanian force takes Yemen, cutting Aksum off from the Arabian trade
Aksum shelters early Muslim emigrants from Arabia
Aksumite coinage ceases after more than three centuries
